sentences.text:
Shri Vishal Vincent Daniel - Advocate with Shri Ankit T
 Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Anil Upadhyay - Panel Lawyer for respondent.
Heard on admission.
Appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.110/2026, which is first application under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 30.12.2025 passed by the learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Tikamgarh, District Tikamgarh (M.P.), in ST No.224/2024, whereby present appellant has been convicted under Sections 467, 468, 471, 120B, 419 and 420 of IPC and sentenced as mentioned therein.

entities.text: 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Tikamgarh, District Tikamgarh (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of present appellant that the present appellant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

As per the prosecution story,
present appellant is the property dealer who has introduced the seller co-accused Parsuram Kewat 2 CRA-110-2026 with the purchaser Krishnakant Agrawal (P.W.3) but the sole witness Krishnakant (PW 3) in this behalf has not named the present appellant in Examination in the trial Court.
In para 7 of his cross examination, he has categorically admitted that he does not know the present appellant Dinesh Richariya.
He cannot identify him.
Therefore, there is no evidence on record against the present appellant.

Though P.W.1 Droupati Ahirwar has stated that Krishnakant Agrawal has filed a complaint before police naming the present appellant as property dealer but Krishnakant Agrawal did not state anything against the present appellant.
Therefore, there is no evidence against him.
Exhibit P/8 is police statement and that cannot be the basis for convicting the present appellant.
It is further submitted that present appellant has a good case on merit.
He has no criminal antecedents.
The final disposal of this appeal will take considerable time.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by the Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of present appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the appellant and prayed for rejection of application.

Having heard the rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties, perused the record and keeping in view the attending facts and circumstances of case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A. No.110/2026 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the entire fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like 3 CRA-110-2026 amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court
, the remaining jail sentence of present appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.

The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 03.08.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard, till final disposal of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
